name: $\vec{F}_{net} = 0$
content: Newton's first law condition for a particle at rest or in motion at constant velocity
e: Newton's first law condition for a particle at rest or in motion at constant velocity is written $\vec{F}_{net} = 0$. Zero net force means constant velocity, including staying at rest.

name: $\vec{F}_{net} = m\vec{a}$
e: Newton's second law of motion is written $\vec{F}_{net} = m\vec{a}$. Net force and acceleration point the same way, and a equals F over m.

name: $\frac{F_{1}}{a_{1}} = \frac{F_{2}}{a_{2}} = m = \text{constant}$
content: Ratio of force magnitude to acceleration magnitude defining the mass of a particle
e: Ratio of force magnitude to acceleration magnitude defining the mass of a particle is written $\frac{F_{1}}{a_{1}} = \frac{F_{2}}{a_{2}} = m = \text{constant}$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

name: $\vec{F}_{\text{second on first}} = -\vec{F}_{\text{first on second}}$
content: Newton's third law of motion (action and reaction)
e: Newton's third law of motion (action and reaction) is written $\vec{F}_{\text{second on first}} = -\vec{F}_{\text{first on second}}$. Action and reaction are equal and opposite, and they act on two different bodies.

name: $1\text{ N} = 1\text{ kg m s}^{-2}$
e: SI unit of force (Newton) is written $1\text{ N} = 1\text{ kg m s}^{-2}$. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

name: $1\text{ dyne} = 1\text{ g cm s}^{-2}$
e: CGS unit of force is written $1\text{ dyne} = 1\text{ g cm s}^{-2}$. Each symbol stands for a quantity from this chapter.

name: $F = G\frac{m_{1}m_{2}}{r^{2}}$
e: Newton's law of gravitation is written $F = G\frac{m_{1}m_{2}}{r^{2}}$. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

name: $\vec{F}_{21} = -\frac{Gm_{1}m_{2}}{r_{21}^{2}}\hat{r}_{21}$
content: Newton's law of gravitation in vector form
e: Newton's law of gravitation in vector form is written $\vec{F}_{21} = -\frac{Gm_{1}m_{2}}{r_{21}^{2}}\hat{r}_{21}$. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

name: $w = mg$
content: Weight of a body as gravitational force
e: Weight of a body as gravitational force is written $w = mg$. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

name: $g = G\frac{M}{R^{2}}$
content: Acceleration due to gravity near the earth's surface
e: Acceleration due to gravity near the earth's surface is written $g = G\frac{M}{R^{2}}$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

name: $v = v_{0} + gt$
content: First equation of motion for free fall
e: First equation of motion for free fall is written $v = v_{0} + gt$. Each symbol stands for a quantity from this chapter.

name: $v^{2} = v_{0}^{2} + 2gh$
content: Second equation of motion for free fall
e: Second equation of motion for free fall is written $v^{2} = v_{0}^{2} + 2gh$. Each symbol stands for a quantity from this chapter.

name: $h = v_{0}t + \frac{1}{2}gt^{2}$
content: Third equation of motion for free fall
e: Third equation of motion for free fall is written $h = v_{0}t + \frac{1}{2}gt^{2}$. Each symbol stands for a quantity from this chapter.

name: $\vec{p} = m\vec{v}$
e: Momentum of a body is written $\vec{p} = m\vec{v}$. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

name: $\vec{p}_{A} + \vec{p}_{B} = \vec{p}_{A}^{\prime} + \vec{p}_{B}^{\prime}$
content: Law of conservation of momentum in vector form
e: Law of conservation of momentum in vector form is written $\vec{p}_{A} + \vec{p}_{B} = \vec{p}_{A}^{\prime} + \vec{p}_{B}^{\prime}$. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

name: $m_{A}\vec{v}_{A} + m_{B}\vec{v}_{B} = m_{A}\vec{v}_{A}^{\prime} + m_{B}\vec{v}_{B}^{\prime}$
content: Conservation of momentum for a two-body collision
e: Conservation of momentum for a two-body collision is written $m_{A}\vec{v}_{A} + m_{B}\vec{v}_{B} = m_{A}\vec{v}_{A}^{\prime} + m_{B}\vec{v}_{B}^{\prime}$. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

name: $m_{B} = m_{A}\frac{v_{A}^{\prime}}{v_{B}^{\prime}}$
content: Measurement of inertial mass using a compressed spring
e: Measurement of inertial mass using a compressed spring is written $m_{B} = m_{A}\frac{v_{A}^{\prime}}{v_{B}^{\prime}}$. You compare the unknown amount with a standard so the result is a number with a unit.
